correctness.rationale: The admissible strict triangle side cone is convex. Set x=p-a,y=p-b,z=p-c>0 and x+y+z=p; homogeneity permits p=1. Direct differentiation of xyz/(x+y+z)^2 gives X=yz(1-2x), Y=xz(1-2y), Z=xy(1-2z), and side gradient ((-X+Y+Z)/2,(X-Y+Z)/2,(X+Y-Z)/2). If every slack is <=1/2, X,Y,Z>=0 and <=1/4; the two possible derivative sign patterns bound l1 gradient by 3/8. If x>1/2, the other two are below half and u=-X,v=Y,w=Z satisfy u+v+w=x(1-x)-yz-2xyz<=1/4; l1 gradient<=3/8. Integrating along the convex cone gives the global d-infinity Lipschitz bound. Along x=epsilon,y=z=(1-epsilon)/2, the side gradient tends to (-1/8,1/8,1/8), and perturbations with its signs are feasible, proving sharp unattained supremum 3/8.
